_meta: TEMPLATE — copy to test-integrity.config.json and tune for THIS project's stack. Drives test-integrity.mjs (the anti-tamper gate). ALL keys are optional; omitting one keeps the built-in JS/TS default. The gate is comment/string-aware: assertion/test-case/skip tokens are counted in CODE only (a token inside a string literal is ignored), and suppression directives are counted in COMMENTS only — so listing a pattern like "@ts-ignore" as a string here or in docs is NOT mistaken for a real suppression.
_base_ref: Ref to diff against. If omitted: merge-base(HEAD, work_branch) (work_branch from reconcile.config.json), then HEAD~1, then HEAD. A degraded base (HEAD~1/HEAD) only sees the last commit, so the autonomous loop (verify runs AFTER the per-task commit) should set this to the integration branch, e.g. "origin/main", so the whole task range is in view.
_excludeGlobs: Paths to SKIP entirely (substring, case-insensitive). The gate protects a PROJECT's tests, not the orchestrator's own tooling or its prose docs (both legitimately contain pattern strings / examples). Add build dirs or generated code here.
_testGlobs: A changed file counts as a TEST when its repo-relative path contains ANY of these substrings (case-insensitive). Python: ["test_", "_test.py", "/tests/"]. Go: ["_test.go"].
_assertionKeywords: Call-site shapes that count as ONE assertion each (anchored to a '(' or '.' to avoid identifier inflation like 'shouldRetry' matching 'should'). A DROP in total across changed test files ⇒ ERROR. pytest: ["assert "]. Go: ["require.", "assert.", ".Errorf("]. JUnit: ["assertThat", "assertEquals("].
_testCaseKeywords: Call-site shapes that count as ONE test case each. DROP ⇒ ERROR. pytest: ["def test_"]. Go: ["func Test"]. JUnit: ["@Test"].
_skipPatterns: Disable/skip/only markers (counted in CODE). INCREASE in total across changed test files ⇒ ERROR (silently disabling judgment). pytest: ["@pytest.mark.skip", "@pytest.mark.xfail"]. Go: ["t.Skip("].
_ignorePatterns: Type/lint suppressions that hide failing checks (counted in COMMENTS only). INCREASE ⇒ ERROR — checked in test AND non-test files. Python: ["type: ignore", "noqa"]. Go: ["nolint"].
_lineComments: Line-comment lead-ins used to separate code from comments. '#' counts as a comment only at a token boundary (so JS private fields like this.#x are not treated as comments). SQL/Lua projects can add "--" (NOT a default — it collides with JS i--).
_testMigrations: Optional exact-path audit records for tests retired by an architectural/IA migration. Each active group must name deleted source tests, existing replacement tests, and a reason. The gate requires replacement aggregate case/assertion counts >= deleted aggregate. Globs are forbidden.
_suppressionAllowances: Optional exact-path, exact-directive audit records for necessary new suppressions. maxIncrease is a hard cap on the net added directives and reason is mandatory. Globs and reason-less allowances are not supported.
_coverageConfigPath: Repo-relative path to the file that holds coverage thresholds. A LOWERED numeric threshold ⇒ ERROR; a deleted file ⇒ ERROR. Examples: "vitest.config.ts", "jest.config.js", "pyproject.toml" (tool.coverage fail_under), ".nycrc", ".coveragerc". Leave null to skip.
_coverageThresholdKeys: Threshold field names to track (matched as `<key> : | = <number>`, key optionally quoted). Kept SPECIFIC (not generic words like 'min'/'global') so prose such as '# minimum node version 20' is not mistaken for a threshold. pytest-cov uses "fail_under"; nyc/jest/vitest use statements/branches/functions/lines.
